all_passages.content: I do crypto mostly — I have about 40% of my savings in crypto. Rest in a couple of mutual funds and some liquid funds for cash management. I also hold about 0.5 grams of digital gold on PhonePe, just experimented with it.
Returns. Plain and simple. FDs give 6-7%, inflation eats that up. Crypto is volatile but the upside is huge. I'm okay with that volatility.
It was fine. Easy to buy. But it just sits there doing nothing — no returns. I just bought it to diversify a bit. Gold doesn't really excite me.
If it gave me returns. Otherwise why not just buy a gold ETF which is more liquid?
Okay now this is interesting. So basically it's like staking but for gold? I do crypto staking and earn 8-12% APY. So 5-7% on gold is actually competitive if the gold price also goes up.
That's actually a good combination. Like, if gold goes up 5% and I also earn 7%, that's 12% total return with less volatility than crypto. I'd consider moving some of my portfolio here.
For me it's a positive actually. I know CoinDCX, I use them for crypto. They're a legit exchange, listed, regulated. More trustworthy than some random fintech I've never heard of.
How liquid is it? Can I exit anytime or is there a lock-in? If there's a lock-in of even 30 days I'd want higher yield — like 8-9%.
Also, how is the 5-7% range decided? Is it variable month to month?
Route 2 definitely. 'Gold that earns more gold every year.' That's a great line. I'd click on that. Route 1 is for my mom, not for me.

Yes, 2.5% annual interest plus gold appreciation. Government backed. But you can't buy them whenever you want — only when the government issues them. And 8-year lock-in. CoinDCX's version would be better if the yield is higher and it's flexible.

Fix the yield transparency — give a floor rate. Add staking-like flexibility (no lock-in or short lock-in). Market it on crypto and investment apps, not just gold apps. I'd put 15-20% of my portfolio here if those things are done.
